cards.back:
Retrieve data from one or more tables.
SELECT column1, column2 FROM table WHERE condition;

Add new rows to a table.
INSERT INTO table (col1, col2) VALUES (val1, val2);

Group rows for aggregate functions.
SELECT department, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY department;

Filter groups (like WHERE but for GROUP BY).
SELECT dept, AVG(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY dept HAVING AVG(salary) > 50000;

Combine rows from two tables where a condition matches.
SELECT * FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id;

All rows from left table + matched rows from right. Unmatched right columns are NULL.
SELECT * FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id;
All rows from right table + matched rows from left. Unmatched left columns are NULL. Opposite of LEFT JOIN.
All rows from both tables. Unmatched columns are NULL on either side. Not supported in MySQL (use UNION of LEFT + RIGHT).

Count rows. COUNT(*) counts all rows. COUNT(column) counts non-NULL values.
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed';

Pattern matching for strings.
% matches any sequence, _ matches one character.
WHERE name LIKE 'J%' — names starting with J.
WHERE code LIKE 'A_B' — A, any char, B.

Combine results from multiple queries.
UNION removes duplicates. UNION ALL keeps all rows.
Queries must have same number and types of columns.

Uniquely identifies each row. Cannot be NULL. One per table. Often auto-incremented.
id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT

References a primary key in another table. Enforces referential integrity.
FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

Conditional logic in queries.
SELECT name,
  CASE WHEN score >= 90 THEN 'A'
       WHEN score >= 80 THEN 'B'
       ELSE 'C' END AS grade
FROM students;
